answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to embed a unique quartz-hard computational fingerprint derived from its private history into every graded answer. New accounts must wander through multiple epochs of original work before any influence accrues, while a glacier-slow reputation accrual makes mass identity creation prohibitively expensive in both time and creative effort. Attackers face linear costs that scale with the number of fakes they spin up.
